title: Bounded-below filtered continuity of pro-etale pushforward
statement: Use small sites and indexing categories as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on profinite sets with the finite jointly surjective topology, and set $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for each scheme $X$, using the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], use the ordinary uncompleted derived pushforward $Rf_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] between module-sheaf categories. Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $(K_i^\bullet)$ a diagram of complexes of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves with one common lower bound $a$ on the cohomology. Write $K_i^{\geq a}=\tau_{\geq a}K_i$ for good truncation and $K=Q(\varinjlim_i K_i^{\geq a})$, where the colimit is termwise in sheaves, and $Q$ is passage to the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every integer $q$ the canonical map $\varinjlim_i H^q(Rf_*QK_i)\to H^q(Rf_*K)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda_Y$-module sheaves. If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the analogous canonical map $\varinjlim_i H^q(R\Gamma(X,QK_i))\to H^q(R\Gamma(X,K))$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. These comparisons are natural in the diagrams and compatible with shifts. Here $R\Gamma$ is derived global sections of module sheaves, computed by injective resolutions. Equivalently, for functorial bounded-below complex representatives of $Rf_*K_i$ or $R\Gamma(X,K_i)$ the termwise filtered colimit maps quasi-isomorphically to a representative of the value at $K$. The assertion is independent of such functorial quasi-isomorphic replacements. Complexes and good truncation are as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Explicitly $\tau_{\geq a}K$ is zero below $a$, is $\operatorname{coker}(d^{a-1})$ in degree $a$, and agrees with $K$ above $a$, with the induced differential.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-local-comparison] at every affine weakly contractible target object. For the underlying abelian-sheaf map, use the covering-family theorem to prove sectionwise injectivity on arbitrary objects by separatedness. On each covering member the map is surjective; the corresponding lifts establish local surjectivity. The Mathlib locally bijective sheaf criterion makes the underlying map invertible, and Mod.forget reflects isomorphisms. This is the complete Lean proof of condensed_qcqs_pushforward_continuity.

For global sections take W=X and the existing affine weakly contractible hypercover. Forget the internal coefficient action and use the already constructed abelian hypercover total and its canonical restriction augmentation. Forgetting preserves bounded-below complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. The existing internal-module injective-row theorem and the abelian bounded-below row comparison prove that the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism on complexes of injective internal modules. The existing abelian column comparison proves that the total inverts bounded-below quasi-isomorphisms.

Apply the generic bounded-below section model to identify actual derived global sections naturally with the forgotten-coefficient abelian hypercover total on strictly bounded-below complexes. The existing total-colimit theorem and preservation by the internal forgetful functor show that this model preserves the filtered colimit. Homology preserves exact filtered colimits. Good truncation is a quasi-isomorphism under the assumed cohomological bound. Transport the colimit cocone along the natural comparison and identify its universal map with the original canonical comparison.

The two shift assertions use the natural isomorphism between shifting a complex before applying Q, the right derived functor and H^q, and applying H^(s+q) directly. Naturality of condensedContinuityComparison conjugates its map by this isomorphism. The unshifted continuity theorem at s+q makes it invertible; connectedness identifies its mapped cocone as a colimit and gives invertibility of colimMap of its legs. No new shifted hypercover computation is needed.
Representative compatibility is proved separately from the assumed comparisons in every degree using homology preservation of exact filtered colimits and the given representative leg equation.
